content: Offset-based pagination against a live, actively-written table causes skipped or duplicated rows as inserts/deletes shift row positions between pages; cursor-based pagination (stable indexed column, e.g. PK) avoids this. Migrating from live production tables also needs an explicit snapshot boundary (e.g. captured max-id watermark, or read-replica/point-in-time read) so that dry-run and apply see a consistent, bounded slice rather than an ever-growing tail of new rows, and so idempotent re-runs converge instead of re-processing new writes as if they were unprocessed backlog.
